title: Rewriting Text in My Own Writing Style
tools: QLoRA (quantized low-rank adaptation) · DPO (direct preference optimization) · vLLM · Qwen3.5-9B / Qwen3.8-27B · Slurm on the OSU (Oregon State University) cluster
blurb: A QLoRA fine-tune that rewrites text in my style from ~20,000 words of my writing; it nudged chrF from 65.0 to 67.5, while preference tuning only memorized.
long: A model that rewrites generic, assistant-style text in my own style. I trained it on ~20,000 words of my finished writing, paired with generic rewrites of the same passages, and held out 5 documents for evaluation.

Scored by chrF (character overlap with my original), leaving the generic text unchanged scores 65.0. Base models moved it further from my writing (56-57), and only the tuned models moved it closer: 67.5 (Qwen3.5-9B) and 67.2 (Qwen3.8-27B). A small gain, as expected from this little data.

DPO (direct preference optimization) on my own A/B ratings memorized the training pairs and scored at chance on held-out ones, so I shelved it. The current step uses an AI-text detector as the reward instead.
highlights: chrF (character n-gram F-score): input 65.0, base model 56-57, few-shot 62-64, tuned 67.2-67.5
27B QLoRA (quantized low-rank adaptation) trains in 29.6 minutes on one 48 GB GPU
DPO (direct preference optimization) v1: 100% train, 50% held-out: memorized, shelved
AI-detector probe: drafts 1.00, tuned rewrites 0.84, my writing 0.08
